name: Ludwig Wittgenstein
summary: Wittgenstein is known for philosophy of logic and language, not political writing. Scholars describe him as anti-political rather than apolitical, with a documented interest in the Soviet Union (a 1935 visit) but no stated positions on the questions this test asks.

sources.title: Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus (Ogden translation, full text)
sources.author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
sources.usedFor: His main early work, read in full for political content: it states none (ethics and the mystical are said to be inexpressible).

sources.title: Wittgenstein and Russia
sources.author: John Moran
sources.usedFor: Surveys his 1935 Soviet visit and the thin evidence on his politics; reports no explicit statement of positions.

sources.title: Ludwig Wittgenstein
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Biographical facts (gave away his share of the family fortune, joined the Austrian army in 1914); states no political views.

sources.title: Wittgenstein in Russia
sources.author: Jared Marcel Pollen
sources.usedFor: Quotes his 1922 and 1935 letters about Russia; a remark of being a Marxist in his heart; presents no formal political commitment.
